steps.text: Whisk honey, Dijon mustard, chili powder, and salt together in a bowl; pour into a resealable plastic bag. Add pork tenderloins, coat with marinade, squeeze out excess air, and seal the bag. Marinate in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium, indirect heat and lightly oil the grate.
Remove tenderloins from marinade and shake off excess. Discard remaining marinade.
Cook on the preheated grill until an instant-read thermometer inserted into centers reads 145 degrees F (63 degrees C), 15 to 25 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Tangy Grilled Pork Tenderloin
raw_recipe.description: This tangy grilled pork tenderloin recipe marinates the tenderloin in honey, Dijon mustard, chili powder, and salt. It’s quick, easy, and flavorful.
raw_recipe.name: Tangy Grilled Pork Tenderloin

review.reviewBody: This pork dish was crazy good! I didn't have access to a grill due to the cold so I opted for the baking it for 40 minutes on 400 degree method and it was fabulous. I followed the recipe to a T but added in minced garlic to the marinade. We thoroughly enjoyed this and enjoyed the sauce it made served over white rice. Thank you for another great one!

Didn’t put chilie powder in because making for a four year old that doesn’t like ANY spices the pork loin came out very flavorful and I made it in a smoker on 220 degrees for 5 1/2 hours until it reached 175 internally. I like honey mustard mixture and this as delicious, family enjoyed it too my daughter cleaned her plate and had seconds.

This is awesome. I used a one pound top loin roast, cut into one inch thick slices. Using a fork, I pierced them well before adding the sauce, marinated them 20 hours, and turned them several times. As the recipe calls for 2 pounds of pork, I had ample marinade and reserved some to use as a serving sauce, and am very glad I did. Delicious! It was very tender and extremely flavorful. When I make this again, I will reduce the honey as we found it a bit too sweet. Can't wait to try it with other pork cuts and perhaps chicken.

I added extra chili powder and a good splash of E. NC bbq sauce to loosen the marinade a bit. I heated up the marinade as well and used it as a sauce. This was delicious and will be a monthly meal at least!

This marinade is absolutely delicious. Made it tonight for a party. I took some other reviewers suggestions and added a little minced garlic and used cayenne pepper verses chili powder. I took the marinade from the bag and boiled it so if someone wanted to add a little more after the pork was cooked we had it ready and safe to eat. Thank you for sharing will definitely make again.

Made this last night for the second time but instead of pork used chicken and it was delicious! Shared it with my neighbor and she loved the marinade.

Wow, really good and easy. I just threw all the ingredients into a crock pot on high for 4 - 5 hours and it was amazing (I didn’t even marinate first).Was a bit sweet for me, so I might try a little less honey next time, but everyone else thought it was perfect.

This is the best basic recipe for marinating a tenderloin. So many ways to change it up to suit your specific taste. Try backing out of the honey and use some lemon juice in place of the dijon, but as is it works well. Pork and dijon were made for each other. I did just that, backed out of the dijon and honey just a bit, added 1/4 cup lemon juice and used a single Chipotle pepper with a teaspoon of the adobo sauce in place of the chile powder. Marinated 6 hours. Unbelievable flavor!!
Always take advantage of the grill time. I like to grill corn on the cob with this tenderloin recipe. Try this... soak the corn, unshucked in whole milk at least overnight but 48 hours is even better. Throw them on the grill unshucked. The soaking keeps them from burning. When the husks begin to turn dark and burn, they are done. Shuck, add salt and pepper and butter. Enjoy!!

I've made this recipe twice now. The first time I had a used a good quality tenderloin but the second time I bought my meat from Costco and it was tough - lesson learned. The only change I made to the recipe was to add garlic and as other reviewers suggested, I boiled the marinade and used it to baste while cooking and to serve along side the meat. Very tasty and easy & I'll definitely make it again.

This recipe was easy and tasted great! The only change I made was instead of pork tenderloin, I used chicken breast halves. I sealed them in a Ziploc and left them to marinate over night. 

My wife and kids loved every bite!

This is so good, especially if you save the marinade and heat it, letting it simmer for 5 minutes. I did have to cook it in the oven as we had no grill in the beach house we were renting and I did double the Dijon mustard but everyone raves about the marinade. Will definitely make again!
This was tasty and unbelievably easy. It did, however, need the remaining marinade as a a sauce. Next time, I will definitely boil the leftover marinade and spoon it over the sliced pork.
The sauce was an odd combination of sweet and tangy and didn't marinate the meat, so it was more of a dipping sauce.
The mustard was overpowering , I cut the mustard amount by half and still found that was all I could taste.
This is my “go to” recipe for pork. It’s simple to make and very flavorful. I boil the marinade and use it to baste the pork on the grill. Then, I serve it on the side.

Very Bland! I marinated the tenderloins for about 16 hours; the marinade just didn’t make much of a difference in flavor. I cooked them in the oven at 400 degrees for about 40 minutes. Would not use this recipe again.
Had a pound and a half pork tenderloin. That I cut in half to season one with Greek seasoning and the other with this recipe.

Very tender and juicy. Marinated for 8 hr and set at room temp about 15 minutes before grilling. Grilled on grates about 4 min per side to get some grill marks and then placed on wood grilling plank for about 40 minutes opening the grill twice to baste with marinate. Internal temp was 154 degrees and I let it rest 10 min before slicing. Served drizzled with remaining marinate (boiled). Tangy... not to my taste buds. Think next time I’ll double or triple the chili powder or maybe whisk in a couple healthy dashes of hot sauce.
Great recipe! Is one of my summer staples. I did add some garlic, green onions, and rosemary as well.
This was very quick and easy to prepare. Came off the grill very tender, and moist. First time I every cooked a pork tenderloin on the grill
YUM! I made it as written, except with half the marinade. I thought there would be too much marinade left over and half was perfect.
